manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Hang the cup on the rack.

Task description: Hang the light-colored cup on the left side of the wooden cup rack from one of its bars. The cup is suspended by its handle, and the bar must pass through the handle opening.

Success criteria: The cup is picked up, its handle is placed over the rack bar and supported by it, and it hangs clear of the table without support from the gripper.

## Execution tips

- Consider gripping an intact cup-wall section at the rim away from the handle, with one finger inside and one outside. Set the opening for thickness and insertion clearance, leaving room for handle-to-rod engagement.
- Before closing, use different views to confirm the fingers are inside and outside the cup wall with ample pad contact rather than merely pressing the rim. Watch for sliding during a small test lift to reduce drops in transit.
- Choose a hanging rod with open space around its free end to fit the cup and gripper. Adjust the handle orientation away from the rack where possible, avoiding nearby rods during rotation.
- For engagement, align the rod's free end with the handle opening and approach in small steps along the rod direction. Observe whether the tip actually enters the opening, avoiding mistaking image overlap for insertion or pushing the rack over with the handle's outer edge.
- Before release, let the handle's inner edge rest on the rod and bear weight, rather than merely catching the tip. Gradually reduce gripper support while checking for sliding, and leave rim clearance when withdrawing fingers to avoid lifting the cup again.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start one real-robot episode with the specified parameters and act on the returned manual and live observations. When finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

I have read the returned manual; only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the approach pose outside the cup stand, preparing to grasp the cup wall through the opening and test the hold with a small lift.

A pose adjustment encountered a recoverable joint limit. I reduced the tilt using the latest measurements and continued approaching. The gripper is now aligned with one side of the cup opening; next I will descend in steps no greater than 1 cm to confirm both finger positions.
The gripper opening has been reduced to about 4 cm. The wrist view shows one finger aimed inside the cup and the other outside. I will lower slightly further, confirm the insertion depth, then close.
I adjusted to a grip with one finger inside and the other outside the cup wall. The cup remains on the table without noticeable movement. Next I will complete the grasp and make a small test lift.

The cup has lifted slightly off the table and remained stable relative to the gripper in two test lifts, with measured gap approximately 3.7 mm. Next I will raise it and approach the lower hanging rod on the left.

The cup remains stable during transport and is near the lower rod on the left. The gripper partly obscures the handle. I will use small motions and both views to locate the rod tip, confirming insertion and load support before release.

The cup handle and rod tip nearly overlap in the main view, but the wrist view has not confirmed that the handle passed over the rod. I will correct the front-back position first rather than treating image overlap as a successful hang.

The rack shifted slightly during pose adjustment, so I retreated outward. The cup remains securely grasped. Next I will correct front-back handle alignment while watching clearance between the upper rod and arm.

The cup rack rotated again during the previous inward movement, indicating contact along the current path; it is not yet hung. I have moved back and am realigning the cup handle from a position closer to the robot.

After withdrawing and adjusting the front-back position, the rod end began to appear on the right side of the wrist view, and the cup stand has not moved further. I am aligning the handle opening to it gradually.
The bar end is near the outside of the cup handle, and both cup and rack remain stable. I will use steps of a few millimeters to attempt insertion and observe whether the handle or rack is pushed.

The rod end has not been confirmed through the handle. The last small approach moved the rack slightly, so I withdrew. Next I will make a small front-back correction and try again while keeping the grasp.

Small forward and backward corrections still result in contact, and the handle has not been confirmed over the rod. I will first move away from the rod, adjust the handle orientation, and seek a clearer view and more clearance for the connection.

The cup handle has been turned by about 15°, and the rod axis appears closer to horizontal in the wrist view. I am correcting the position of the opening center relative to the rod end, then approaching slowly along the rod axis.

After reorientation, the rod tip still contacts near the handle edge without entering. I will retreat, lift the mug slightly and check for a height mismatch. If safe engagement remains uncertain, I will replace the mug on the table and end the episode.

The small approach after lifting did not push the rack further. The bar end is now in the occluded area of the cup handle. Insertion through the hole and whether the handle can bear the weight still need confirmation; the gripper has not been released.

The wrist view now clearly shows the wooden rod end inside the cup handle opening. Next I will insert it slightly farther and lower a little to let the handle bear the weight, then gradually release after confirming support.

The wooden bar end has now passed through the cup handle hole, and the cup is still partly supported by the gripper. I am lowering slightly and preparing to reduce the grip so the handle gradually bears the weight.

The tool rejected the release command: the operator authorization period cannot cover the next complete action, and the episode entered a safety pause. I will send no further motion commands and immediately call finish_episode. The cup has been lifted, and the rod tip is visibly through its handle, but the gripper has not released it and independent hanging remains unverified.
